title: feat(spec): optional caller on IAutomationService.toggleFlow
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBXVayMXFjUu7EtXTKCGj4pc)_

Fixes #26506

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`IAutomationService.toggleFlow` 增加可选的第三个参数 `caller`,只携带 `userId`,用来告诉服务是谁开关了这个打包流程。
- 为什么改:管理员关掉打包流程时,激活台账行与审计行的操作人都是空,审计无法说明是哪位管理员做的;服务端修复 (#26474) 需要契约先有这个通道。
- 风险与回滚:参数可选,现有实现与调用方原样编译,运行时行为零变化;回滚即还原这一行签名。
- 先看:`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`(`toggleFlow` 签名与 TSDoc),`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-toggle-flow-caller.pin.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/contracts/automation-toggle-flow-caller.pin.test.ts`,预期 2 个用例通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`IAutomationService.toggleFlow?(name, enabled)` gains an optional third parameter, `caller`, typed as `Pick` over `AutomationContext` narrowed to the single key `'userId'`. A door that serves a person passes that person's id, so the `sys_metadata_activation` row the switch writes, and its `sys_audit_log` row, can name the admin instead of a null actor. The method's TSDoc now says what the channel carries, that it is attribution only (it grants nothing, and an implementation neither refuses nor widens the switch on it), and that an absent caller, or one with no `userId`, means an unattributed write.

The parameter is optional, so every current implementer (`AutomationEngine.toggleFlow` in `@objectstack/service-automation`) and every caller (the runtime's `POST /api/v1/automation/:name/toggle` door and its test doubles) compiles unchanged. This is the contract half only: the door passing the caller and the engine writing with it are the server half, #26474.

## Why this shape

The order was to follow `execute(flowName, context?: AutomationContext)` in the same contract, reusing `AutomationContext` or a narrow subset of it. I took the subset, one key:

- **`userId` is the key the write records.** The engine stamps `created_by` / `updated_by` from the context's user, and the audit writer reads `user_id` from it. `AutomationContext.userId` is already the contract's spelling for "the acting user", so `execute` and `toggleFlow` name the person the same way.
- **No positions, permissions or posture.** `toggleFlow` is no authority gate: ADR-0126 §5 gates the switch at the door that receives the request, and the ledger write runs elevated. A channel carrying grants would invite a second gate inside the service whose rules could drift from the door's.
- **No tenant.** The activation ledger is deployment state with no organization column (ADR-0126 as amended by ADR-0131 D6), so a tenant id would carry nothing the write reads.
- **Not the whole `AutomationContext`.** Most of its keys (`record`, `params`, `runAs`, `flowName`, `flowRunId`, `callerParamKeys`) describe a run and mean nothing for a switch. Taking the whole type would leave each implementer to decide which to ignore. With the narrow type, a caller literal carrying `positions` or `record` does not compile (pinned).
- **Not `ExecutionContext`.** Several store contracts take the caller as `ExecutionContext | undefined` (`IAIConversationService`, `ISharingService`). That would hand the service the caller's whole principal, grants included, which is the second-gate risk above. The order also pointed at the `AutomationContext` precedent in this contract.

Widening later is additive: another key can join the `Pick` if a reader ever needs it.

## Tests

`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-toggle-flow-caller.pin.test.ts`, compiled by `check:test-typecheck` under `tsconfig.test.json` and run by vitest:

- type level: the third parameter is exactly the narrowed `Pick` or `undefined`; the arity is 2 or 3; `name` and `enabled` keep their types and places;
- additive: a two-parameter implementation (a function and a class) still satisfies the contract, and a two-argument call still compiles;
- narrow: a caller literal with `positions`, or with `record`, is a compile error (`@ts-expect-error`, which itself fails if the line ever compiles);
- runtime: an implementation reads `caller?.userId` without a cast, and reads it as absent when not passed; a two-parameter implementation runs when a caller is passed.

Reverse verification (one-off, not kept): the signature reverted to the two-parameter form via `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob `8fc1e1cc` to `201b1e11`), then `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`. The pin file turned red with 9 errors (TS2344 on both identity asserts, TS2554 on each three-argument call, TS2493 and TS7006 where the third parameter vanished). Restored: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Acceptance notes

- Until #26474's server half lands, the flow switch still writes a null actor; this PR changes no runtime behaviour.
- The runtime tests that pin the door's call as `toHaveBeenCalledWith(FLOW, false)` (`automation-activation-posture-gate.test.ts`, `http-dispatcher.test.ts`) will need the caller argument when the door starts passing it. That is the server half's edit, noted here so it is not a surprise.
- A non-human caller (an agent or service principal) has no `actor` label on this channel; `AutomationContext` declares none. No reader needs one today.
